done_when: When the page cannot get new data, one line under the header gives the reason and the next step, and a failed read while the server runs says the work could not be read instead of Offline.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done - A plan read can fail while its old contents remain marked Live with no explanation.
Case: normal use - A person has opened a story's Plan tab, then a later plan request fails while the snapshot stream remains healthy. The plan request can fail independently, for example when local and published plan edits conflict (src/forge/story.py:624). The new read hook does not cover the direct fetch at src/forge/board_app/item.js:397, and item.js:409-410 silently retains the previously read plan. This is new evidence against the earlier assumption that this path always displays its error in place.
findings.title: Not done: Show failed reads of a story's plan

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done - The line says the page tries again, but an initial item failure can leave both the error and the line on screen indefinitely.
Case: normal use - A person opens a direct item link or an older part and its first item request fails temporarily. The timer calls snapshot listeners here, but src/forge/board_app/item.js:456-463 only refreshes an item page that already has a row and does not repeat a failed drawer read. Once the server can answer again, neither the item nor its warning recovers without navigation or reopening it.
findings.title: Not done: Retry an item's first failed read

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done - A connected page can keep showing a reason that has already been fixed.
Case: normal use - Two stories have conflicting local and published plan edits. After the first conflict is resolved, the next rebuild can fail on the other story. This comparison emits a failure event only when the error changes between present and absent; it sends nothing when one error replaces another. The page therefore continues naming the first conflict until a rebuild succeeds or the stream reconnects, even though the server's current reason is different.
findings.title: Not done: Update the reason when a rebuild fails for a different cause

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 2, Harm 2
Case: normal use - A person closes a failed item drawer, or leaves Releases while its read is still in progress. Closing the drawer does not trigger this hash-change cleanup, and a response that fails after navigation calls lose() and adds the departed page's failure back. The retry then targets the current view, so the obsolete warning can remain even after the displayed data is healthy. This is new evidence beyond the ruling that leaving a page forgets its failure.
findings.title: Follow-up: Discard failures belonging to views that have been left

why: The board looks live when its data is old: a stopped server, a failed read and a restart all leave only a small grey Offline word, and after a restart the old page stays Offline because the new board has a new address.
